answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique staking reward compounding record flips the bet — rewards compounded weekly for two years — and the canyon lands on the attacker instead. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that rewards compounded weekly for two years — so privacy survives, and the vertex is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The lantern grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
